answer.exemplar: Inside a metal the electrons are free to move, so any excess charge left in the bulk would be acted on by the field it helps to create and would move. That movement continues until no charge remains free to move, and the state in which nothing further moves is precisely what electrostatic equilibrium means. The surplus charge therefore cannot occupy the interior; it moves out to the surface, where it produces a field outside the metal and none inside it, so the arrangement is self-consistent.

That is a dynamical argument, not merely a statement of fact: equilibrium is defined by the absence of further motion, and any interior charge guarantees motion.
